title: Whose wealth, whose greed
literal_meaning: Whoever owns the wealth owns the greed.
meaning_odia: ଧନ ଯାହାର, ଲୋଭ ମଧ୍ୟ ତାହାର ବୋଲି ଏହି ସଂକ୍ଷିପ୍ତ କଥା କହେ। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ ଧନ ଥିବା ଓ ତାହା ପ୍ରତି ଆସକ୍ତିକୁ ଏହା ଏକାଠି ରଖେ। କାହାର କେତେ ଧନ ବା କେଉଁ ଜିନିଷ ପାଇଁ ଲୋଭ ମୂଳରେ ନାହିଁ; ସବୁ ସମ୍ପତ୍ତିଧାରୀଙ୍କ ଚରିତ୍ର ବିଷୟରେ ଏହା ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ।
explanation: The matching phrases make greed seem another possession belonging to the wealth-holder. Our editorial reading notices the attachment that can accompany having something, rather than assuming that possession ends desire. The saying compresses that observation into a generalisation; it supplies no measure of wealth or particular act of greed.
usage_example: Original imagined example: The owner of a well-stocked store cannot bear to part with a small surplus. Someone recalls this pairing of possession and greed.
cultural_context: The force lies in the mirrored possessives ଯା’ର and ତା’ର. Wealth is named first, and greed follows as though it belonged in the same account.
